invariant: A LOCAL LABEL SUCH AS (a), (b), (1), (A) DOES NOT DETERMINE STRUCTURAL LEVEL BY ITSELF. Its level is resolved from structural context: the ancestor stack, the neighboring label sequence, the enclosing clause syntax (reference lead-ins / spelled numerals / conjunction chains), local list continuation (hanging paragraphs), and source boundaries (line starts, list punctuation).

implementation.name: legal numbering grammar - inline references and spelled numerals are not labels
implementation.code: isInlineReferenceMarker + structuralMarkerOccurrences (reference status propagates along ', / and / or / through' chains)

implementation.name: list continuation / source boundaries - a NEW label family after a hanging paragraph attaches to the enclosing level
implementation.code: hasHangingParagraph + 'if (hangingParagraphBefore && stack.length >= 2) stack.length -= 1' before a start marker is pushed; continuations of the innermost list are unaffected; page-marker lines and the next label never count as prose

implementation.name: neighboring label sequence - a label continues the NEAREST open list of its family; inline enumeration never re-opens a distant outer subsection
implementation.code: outer-resume skipped when the marker is mid-line, joined by a bare comma/conjunction (not ';'/':'), and a nearer open list of the same family exists

implementation.name: comma exclusion limited to horizontal whitespace
implementation.code: MARKER_OCCURRENCE lookbehind (?<!,[ \t]) so 'without duplication,\n(a) franchise ...' (label on a new line after a lead-in ending in a comma) is a label
